dispositions.topic_text: Construction and concrete contents of the alternate class-policy test release
dispositions.what: How the Factory builds the test release whose class tables differ from the first release's in one row (a test-only data-provider fixture, constants injected at assembly, or parameterised generation), never selectable in production; every option keeps A09 rule 4: an answer above the token's highest class is refused whole.
keeps:
An answer that would carry a class above the
   token's highest is refused whole; Registry never answers part of it.
options: Generate a complete test-only data-provider fixture and assemble an alternate release from it.
Inject alternate constant tables while assembling the verification release.
Parameterize release generation from a Factory fixture.
consequences: A complete fixture exercises release assembly but adds fixture-generation work.
Injection is smaller but requires proof that production cannot select the replacement.
Parameterized generation is reusable but introduces a Factory-owned fixture interface.

dispositions.topic_text: Dedicated owner-interface host, DNS, TLS, and routing configuration
dispositions.what: As round-120 T28: the owner interface's own host name — its DNS or VPN-local name, TLS certificate and routing (TLS at Registry, a reverse proxy routing only that name, or a VPN-local name) — chosen by the Factory's platform deployment; every option keeps A13 rule 1: no other HTTPS service of the host answers under that name or receives the owner session cookie (decided under the owner's direction of 2026-11-24, matrix P6).
keeps:
the deployment gives the owner interface a host name of its
   own, under which no other HTTPS service answers — on the home server not
   the kernel workplace, the gateway or PresuPro — and no other service of
   the same host receives the owner session cookie.
options: Use a dedicated private DNS name with TLS terminated directly at Registry.
Use a dedicated private DNS name at a reverse proxy that routes only that name to Registry.
Use a dedicated VPN-local or hosts-file name with a locally managed certificate.
consequences: Direct termination minimizes routing components but makes Registry's deployment responsible for the certificate endpoint.
A reverse proxy centralizes TLS but must preserve exclusive routing for the hostname.
A VPN-local or hosts-file name avoids public DNS but increases client resolution and certificate administration.

dispositions.topic_text: Factory method for creating and verifying the confirmation-time collision without prescribing hidden implementation seams or function names
dispositions.what: How the Factory shows A16 Required test 13 — a confirmation whose mapping, built in the confirming transaction, is not clean is refused whole — when no surface can choose a minted id (replacing the random source in an executable check, an instrumented build, a structural check that the mapping is built and checked inside the confirming transaction, or both); every option keeps A16 rule 6.
keeps:
A confirmation whose mapping, built in the confirming transaction, is
    not clean is refused whole and nothing changes
options: Replace the random provider during an executable check and exercise confirmation through its public surface.
Use a Factory-only instrumented build that returns a prescribed UUID.
Use a structural gate proving that mapping construction and the clean check occur inside the confirming transaction.
Require both executable collision evidence and a structural transaction-order check.
consequences: Provider replacement follows the admissible history but couples the check to module wiring.
An instrumented build isolates the seam but must be shown equivalent to production generation.
A structural gate checks placement without executing the history and depends on generated-code structure.
Using both gives complementary evidence but adds two checks with distinct responsibilities.

dispositions.topic_text: Verification that the backup instant is read when the first store read fixes the snapshot
dispositions.what: As round-120 T4: how the Factory shows that a backup's instant is read at the read that fixes its snapshot (instrumented clock and store, a structural snapshot path, or both); every option keeps A18 rule 1.
options: Instrument clock and store calls with distinct readings.
Require a structurally approved snapshot-opening path.
Combine structural enforcement with an ordering test.
consequences: The Factory must distinguish a clock read at snapshot fixation from a later read.
